question: In your research system, the web search subagent has two tools, search_news and search_academic. Each tool has the same one-line description: "Searches for sources on a topic." Logs show that the same query goes to search_news in some runs and to search_academic in others, and both tools have valid input schemas. Which change most directly addresses the cause of this unreliable selection?

options.text: Expand both descriptions to state which sources each tool covers, which queries it suits, and when to use the other tool instead.
options.reason: Tool descriptions are the primary mechanism the model uses to select tools, and minimal, identical descriptions give it no basis to choose reliably between similar tools.

options.text: Set tool_choice to "any" so that the subagent must call a tool on every turn and the variation between runs disappears.
options.reason: The "any" option only forces the model to call some tool and does nothing to help it choose between two tools whose descriptions are identical.

options.text: Add more required fields and stricter types to both input schemas so that the model can rely on the schemas alone to tell the two search tools apart.
options.reason: Input schemas define the parameters of a call, but the description is the primary basis for tool selection, so stricter schemas leave the identical descriptions and the unreliable choice in place.

options.text: Add a PostToolUse hook that checks each search result after the call and reruns the query with the other search tool when the result looks weak.
options.reason: The hook reacts after a wrong choice has already been made and leaves the minimal descriptions, which are the cause of the unreliable selection, unchanged.
